title: Formula refusal for date-time subtraction names only whole-day helpers; an hour span (overtime hours) has no named form, though `datetime(a) - datetime(b)` works
body:
Filing category: ① product defect (authoring guidance).
reach: public entries `/api/v1/mcp` `apply_blueprint` (verification) and `validate_expression`, measured on a hosted tenant (`pnpm dev:stack --with-ui`; cloud `ff373e02`, framework `d7c3d44e`).

## Business reason

"Overtime hours = end − start" is a first-day formula for any HR app. The refusal sends the author to `daysBetween`, which cannot express 3.5 hours, and the working form is undiscoverable without reading `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`.

## What happens

- Formula `double((record.end_time - record.start_time).getMinutes()) / 60.0` on two `datetime` fields → `invalid_expression: date arithmetic DateText - DateText … Use daysBetween(a, b) for the span in whole days, and daysFromNow(n) / addDays(d, n) / addMonths(d, n) to shift a date.` (also the wording of migration entry 18.formula-date-subtraction-refused).
- `double((datetime(record.end_time) - datetime(record.start_time)).getMinutes()) / 60.0` → `validate_expression ok: true, inferredType: number`; at runtime the field reads 3, 10, 3.5, 2 on four records — correct.

## Expected

The refusal (and the formula docs / AI rule) names the sub-day form — wrap each side in `datetime(…)` and read the Duration (`.getMinutes()` / `.getHours()`), or a helper such as `hoursBetween(a, b)` — next to `daysBetween`. If the `datetime()` form is not meant to be supported, the validator refuses it too.

Reader who acts: the formula seat (`packages/formula` validate / stdlib, refusal text).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue date-text-arithmetic hours datetime` → 0.
